narrative.overview: A white counter with nothing on it but the thing you came to do. A light grey column beside a white page, one large quiet heading, one central action in a soft pill, and content in pale tinted tiles or between hairlines. Nothing is raised: no cards, no borders around groups, no shadows, no glass. Structure comes from three tones, generous space, and a single hairline where a list needs rows. The front desk is the reason: a receptionist should see one thing, the command bar. Owners at a laptop get the same calm at working density.
keyCharacteristics: White page, grey side: #ffffff next to #fafafa; the tonal step is the only frame.
Near-black ink at 400 and 500: headings are light and large; emphasis comes from size and space.
Pills for every control and every active state.
One dark pill per screen: the primary action is the only solid dark control in view.
Tinted tiles carry glanceable content: five pastels at equal lightness, dark ink on all.
Hairlines, never boxes: rows separate with a 1 px line; nothing is wrapped in a container.
Zero elevation: no shadows, no blur, no surface borders; overlays use a 25 % ink scrim.

rules.name: The One Dark Rule
rules.body: Encre is the only solid dark control on a screen, and there is one of it.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: Active means "sits on a pilule". No underlines, colour changes, or bold for selection.

rules.name: The Tile Rule
rules.body: Tints hold glanceable content only; never forms, tables, or dialogs; never a border or shadow.

rules.name: The Light Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings are 400 or 500. If one needs to be bolder to be seen, give it space instead.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: French sentence case everywhere. No uppercase, no tracked labels.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any value someone compares or reads back renders with tabular figures.

rules.name: The No-Elevation Rule
rules.body: box-shadow, backdrop-filter, and container borders are prohibited. Separate with space, tone, or a hairline between rows.

rules.name: The No-Box Rule
rules.body: Content is never wrapped in a bordered or shadowed card.

dos: Do open hub screens with one light heading and the command bar, centred, with nothing competing.
Do keep exactly one dark pill per screen; every other control is outline, soft, or ghost.
Do mark active states with the grey pill and nothing else.
Do separate rows with hairlines and sections with space; wrap nothing in a card.
Do use the five tints for glanceable content, rotating by position, with dark ink on top.
Do hold text at APCA Lc 75 for body and Lc 60 for labels, verified on the surface it sits on.
Do keep touch targets at 2.75rem, the 3 px focus ring visible, and reduced-motion honoured.
donts: Don't add a shadow, a blur, or a border around a group.
Don't use a second dark control, a coloured button, or a coloured underline for selection.
Don't set a heading above 500 weight or a row label above 600.
Don't use uppercase, tracked labels, or the retired eyebrow.
Don't put a form, a table, or a dialog inside a tinted tile.
Don't use a gradient anywhere except the optional lavis wash behind a hub heading.
Don't revert to the bone ground, drenched surfaces, or 750/800 weights of the previous system.
